main_body: A church pew seen from the east/west side: a tall brown backrest strip on the left and a seat section on the right holding a red cushion panel, with a thin brown seat strip at the bottom.
top_band: none. The column through the middle of the seat runs from a dark outline (row 13) to a thin light-brown rim (rows 14-15), then straight into the red cushion face (rows 16-25). No horizontal surface is visible from above.
evidence: The pew is a side profile: a tall back strip beside a seat/cushion body. The seat top is only a 2-row light brown rim (rows 14-15) above the red face, and a second thin brown band around rows 27-28 reads as a divider, not a surface. The red cushion panels are drawn face-on as vertical faces. There is no seat surface seen from above, so this matches the guide's side elevation chair and thin-seat failures.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown, tinted toward the wood, which is acceptable. The wood has only about 3 tones (dark, mid, light), and the red cushions are large flat fills of one or two reds (roughly 7x9 px) with no grain, speckle or per-element highlights. The back strip is a flat brown column. Compared with the stall and well references, which have tile scallops, stone shading and plank grain, the tiles carry only 2-4 colours each. It is clearly thinner and flatter than the reference.
